action: Opened pmcro-orchestrator.zip via ZipFile.OpenRead and inspected .Entries.FullName; found backslash-separated internal paths (e.g. '.claude-plugin\plugin.json') produced by Compress-Archive on Windows. Backslash is not a valid zip entry path separator per the zip spec, which is what Cowork's validator was rejecting as 'invalid characters'.
Authored scripts/New-PluginZip.ps1 in the repo: builds each zip file-by-file via ZipFile.Open/CreateEntryFromFile, normalizing every entry name to forward slashes.

First run of the new script failed: a relative -OutFile resolved against the process's real working directory (C:\WINDOWS\system32) rather than PowerShell's Set-Location target, because .NET file APIs don't follow PowerShell's location. Fixed by resolving OutFile through GetUnresolvedProviderPathFromPSPath before calling ZipFile.Open.

Re-ran the corrected script: rebuilt pmcro-orchestrator.zip (5413 bytes, 8 files) and pmcro-trail.zip (8414 bytes, 9 files); reopened both and confirmed every entry uses forward slashes with .claude-plugin/plugin.json present at the archive root.
